learning_objective: 🎯 Master the molecular tools of genetic engineering! Learn how scientists literally cut, copy, and paste DNA to create Genetically Modified Organisms.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: These are special enzymes isolated from bacteria that inspect a DNA molecule and cut it ONLY at specific 'palindromic' sequences. This allows scientists to precisely cut out a gene of interest.

Plasmids (extra circular DNA from bacteria) act as vehicles. We cut the plasmid and our gene of interest with the *same* restriction enzyme so they have matching 'sticky ends'. DNA ligase acts as glue to seal them together, creating Recombinant DNA.

The recombinant plasmid is forced into a host bacterium (like E. coli). We use 'Selectable Markers' (like antibiotic resistance genes) to easily identify and isolate only the bacteria that successfully took up our new DNA.

A machine that acts as a DNA photocopier! Through repeated cycles of Denaturation (heating), Annealing (cooling to attach primers), and Extension (building DNA), it amplifies a single copy of DNA into billions of copies in hours.

Once the genetically modified bacteria produce the desired protein (like insulin) in giant tanks called Bioreactors, the product must be carefully separated, purified, and formulated before it can be sold as a medicine.

fun_activity.title: ✂️ The Palindrome Puzzle
fun_activity.instructions: Restriction enzymes cut at Palindromes—sequences that read the same forward and backward on opposite strands. Try writing one! (Example: 5'-GAATTC-3' on top, and 3'-CTTAAG-5' on the bottom). This specific sequence is cut by the famous enzyme EcoRI!

exam_tips: 📌 Memorize the three steps of PCR in order: Denaturation, Annealing, and Extension. Know the function of *Taq* polymerase (it survives high heat).
📌 Be able to draw and label the parts of the pBR322 cloning vector (origin of replication, antibiotic resistance genes, and restriction sites).
📌 Gel Electrophoresis separates DNA fragments strictly by their size. Smaller fragments move faster and further toward the positive anode.
quick_recap: ⭐ Plasmids are autonomously replicating, extra-chromosomal circular DNA found naturally in bacteria.
⭐ DNA is a negatively charged molecule, which is why it moves toward the positive electrode in gel electrophoresis.
⭐ The letters in a restriction enzyme's name come from the bacteria it was isolated from (e.g., EcoRI comes from *E. coli*).
